summary: FEATURED IMAGE — PHASE 3 VALIDATION (baseline v175 + newly added ✳️ star header icon). Verified on live preview URL (https://color-task-timer.preview.emergentagent.com) via Playwright + real JPEG upload against a freshly-created note (TEST_Phase3_StarNote). VERDICT: PASS. The new ✳️ Sparkle button renders in the FullScreenNote header immediately to the LEFT of translate/share/menu (all still visible & enabled), driven by <FeaturedImageBanner variant='star' …/> mounted only when `onSaveInline && note?.id`. Empty-state (no image) — the star opens the picker directly (single Add action). With-image state — the star opens a shadcn DropdownMenu with 'Change Image' and 'Remove Image' items. Upload persists featured_image to IndexedDB and populates the files store. Change replaces attachment_id AND evicts the previous blob (files store size stays at 1). Remove clears note.featured_image to null and evicts the blob (files store size back to 0); the star reverts to Add mode automatically. Title, content (13 chars) and category remained untouched across Add / Change / Remove. Header icons (fullscreen-translate-btn, fullscreen-share-btn, fullscreen-save-status) all remain visible / enabled and share was clicked and closed without regression.

critical_code_review_comments: The star variant cleanly reuses handleFile / handleRemove — no duplication of the persistence pipeline. Good separation.

FullScreenNote now mounts TWO FeaturedImageBanner instances simultaneously (hero body + star header). Both render a hidden <input data-testid='featured-image-file-input'>, so the DOM has two elements with the same data-testid. Test scripts that use CSS/testid selectors without .nth() may pick the wrong one; not a user-facing bug (each input drives the same handleFile against the same parent state), but a testability nit — consider suffixing the input testid with the variant (e.g. featured-image-file-input-star / featured-image-file-input-hero).
The dropdown-menu import path (../components/ui/dropdown-menu) is consistent with other usages in the file — no ESM path issues.
pulseStar visual acknowledgment is short-lived (550ms) and driven by inline style transform+drop-shadow — no reflow, no layout shift, matches existing header icon interaction language.
Star button applies isDark-aware yellow-500/600 palette identical to the existing header icons (translate/share) — visually consistent.
